Talk to us Our solutions At a glance Since 2013 01 Incorporated in Bangalore in 2013 02 Founded by IT and telecom leaders 03 Offices in six countries 04 Cloud, security, networking and managed services Inspire · Innovate · Transform Who we are Built by people who have run infrastructure for a living. bits&BYTE IT Consulting was founded in Bangalore in 2013 by a group of IT and telecom professionals. Today we work from offices in six countries across India, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific. We work from a simple view. Most outages and security incidents do not start inside one system. They start in the gaps: between the team that designed it and the team that runs it, between the network and the cloud, between a firewall rule and the person who forgot why it exists. So we stay with what we build. The same partner assesses the environment, designs the change, delivers it and then operates and monitors it day to day. Fewer handovers mean fewer gaps. Our mission Build infrastructure that is secure, resilient and simple enough to run well, so the business can grow without its technology holding it back. Building the infrastructure behind them is where the work is. bits&BYTE Engineering 18 Oct 2026 9 min read Log stream NTP · NIC / NPL --:--:-- IST Firewall Router Server +04:12 ±0 ms Cloud 1 clock drifting · timeline out of order 4 / 4 clocks in sync · timeline in order Logs kept 180 days Report within 6 hours Time source NIC / NPL On this page Three short rules with a lot behind them Why the clocks come first A time design that holds up 180 days of logs, kept in India Six hours starts before the incident A short readiness check In brief Clocks come first: unsynced logs cannot be put in order, so they cannot tell the story of an incident. Every ICT system’s logs must be kept securely for a rolling 180 days, within Indian jurisdiction. The six-hour reporting window only works if logs are already central, searchable and trusted. Three short rules with a lot behind them On 28 April 2022 CERT-In, India’s national cyber incident response agency, issued Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act. They apply to service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations, and they took effect 60 days after issue. As of October 2026 they are still in force.
